subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Does an untrusted browser origin currently reach a specific mutating Gateway or plugin HTTP handler without satisfying the existing Gateway authentication, origin, and admin-scope checks?
rationale: The named ACP files are not the alleged HTTP surface, but only a security owner should decide whether a privately supplied reproduction demonstrates a real boundary bypass and whether it requires advisory handling.

options.title: Request exact private reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open while requesting a redacted request transcript and endpoint-specific proof through the repository's security-reporting path.

options.title: Route confirmed bypass privately
options.body: If maintainers reproduce a boundary bypass, move technical exploit details into a private advisory and implement the narrow Gateway or plugin-route fix there.

options.title: Close unsupported report
options.body: If no concrete browser-reachable mutating endpoint can be identified after security triage, close the report as unsupported by current source and behavior.

recommendation.title: Request exact private reproduction
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while requesting a redacted request transcript and endpoint-specific proof through the repository's security-reporting path.

likelyOwner.reason: Current repository guidance connects this person to both Gateway and security work, the two areas needed for the boundary decision.
